Implementation using different DS.theory: Stack is LIFO: push/pop at the same end. Queue is FIFO: append at tail, remove at head. Use ArrayDeque in Java 8 for both. For stack call push/pop/peek; for queue offer/poll/peek. ArrayDeque prohibits null. Array-based fixed-capacity implementations must detect overflow and underflow; a circular queue tracks size to distinguish empty/full when head==tail. Linked structures allocate nodes and update empty head/tail cases. See the six concrete implementation lessons below.

Implement Stack using Arrays.problem: Implement the named integer data structure; empty removal throws NoSuchElementException.
Implement Stack using Arrays.approach: Top is the next free array index minus one; push increments size and pop decrements it.
Implement Stack using Arrays.complexity: Array/linked primitives O(1) each; queue-via-two-stacks O(1) amortized with O(n) worst transfer; stack-via-one-queue push O(n), pop O(1). O(capacity) fixed-array or O(n) dynamic storage.
Implement Stack using Arrays.trace: Insert 1 then 2: a stack removes 2; a queue removes 1.
Implement Stack using Arrays.pitfalls: No sentinels collide with valid integer values. Array capacity overflow throws; linked/collection storage grows dynamically.

Implement Queue using Arrays.problem: Implement the named integer data structure; empty removal throws NoSuchElementException.

Balanced Paranthesis.approach: A closing delimiter must match the most recent unmatched opening delimiter, so LIFO is the correct invariant. No openings may remain at end.
Balanced Paranthesis.trace: { then [ then ( are pushed; ),],} pop the matching reverse order.
Balanced Paranthesis.pitfalls: Matching counts alone do not ensure correct nesting: ([)] is invalid.

Infix to Postfix Conversion.problem: Convert valid binary expressions with SINGLE-character operands, operators +,-,*,/,^ and parentheses where applicable. ^ denotes right-associative exponentiation for this parser, not Java XOR.
Infix to Postfix Conversion.approach: Infix uses an operator stack by precedence, popping equal precedence except for right-associative ^. Prefix/postfix conversion scans in the appropriate direction and combines the two operand expressions in their original left/right order.
Infix to Postfix Conversion.complexity: Infix-to-postfix O(n) time/space; string-building conversions can be O(n²) worst time/storage due to immutable intermediate concatenations. Expression trees/StringBuilder traversals can improve output construction.
Infix to Postfix Conversion.trace: a+b*c groups multiplication before addition: postfix abc*+, prefix +a*bc, fully parenthesized infix (a+(b*c)).
Infix to Postfix Conversion.pitfalls: Unary minus and multi-character tokens are outside the grammar. The parser assumes a valid infix token sequence; it checks mismatched parentheses and conversion stack underflow.

Next Greater Element.problem: For each entry return nearest strictly greater value to its right; absent=-1. Return values, not indices.
Next Greater Element.approach: Scan backwards; pop candidates that cannot beat the current value. Each popped candidate is also hidden for any future earlier position by the closer current value. A double scan makes one full circular suffix visible.
Next Greater Element.complexity: O(n) time/space because each pushed entry pops at most once.
Next Greater Element.trace: For [2,1,3], next greater values are 3,3,none; next smaller are 1,none,none.
Next Greater Element.pitfalls: Strict comparison requires popping equals. The value -1 is ambiguous for arbitrary signed arrays; indices or OptionalInt can represent absence unambiguously.
Next Greater Element.alternatives: Scanning each suffix separately takes O(n²) time.

Next Greater Element - 2.problem: For each entry return nearest strictly greater value to its right with wraparound; absent=-1. Return values, not indices.
Next Greater Element - 2.approach: Scan backwards; pop candidates that cannot beat the current value. Each popped candidate is also hidden for any future earlier position by the closer current value. A double scan makes one full circular suffix visible.
Next Greater Element - 2.complexity: O(n) time/space because each pushed entry pops at most once.
Next Greater Element - 2.trace: For [2,1,3], next greater values are 3,3,none; next smaller are 1,none,none.

Next Greater Element - 2.alternatives: Scanning each suffix separately takes O(n²) time.

Asteroid Collision.problem: Nonzero signed asteroids move right if positive, left if negative. Colliding smaller magnitude disappears; equal magnitudes both disappear.
Asteroid Collision.approach: Only a positive survivor immediately before an incoming negative can collide. Pop smaller positives repeatedly; stop when the incoming asteroid dies or no collision pair remains.
Asteroid Collision.trace: Incoming -5 meets 10 and dies; 5 and 10 stay in original order.
Asteroid Collision.pitfalls: Abs(MIN_VALUE) needs long. Negative followed by positive moves apart and never collides.

Sum of Subarray Minimums.problem: Sum every nonempty subarray's minimum, modulo 1e9+7. Values are nonnegative and aggregate contribution fits long under typical n<=30000,a[i]<=30000 bounds.
Sum of Subarray Minimums.approach: Monotone stack assigns each index a previous strictly-smaller boundary and next smaller-or-equal boundary. That asymmetric tie rule gives each subarray one owning minimum. Its contribution is value*(left choices)*(right choices).
Sum of Subarray Minimums.trace: For 1 at index 1 in [3,1,2,4], left choices 2 and right choices 3 give contribution 6; all indices sum to 17.
Sum of Subarray Minimums.pitfalls: Tie asymmetry prevents duplicate ownership. For unconstrained large values/lengths, reduce modular products during accumulation to avoid long overflow.

Sum of Subarray Ranges.problem: Sum max-min of every nonempty subarray, assuming total fits signed long.
Sum of Subarray Ranges.approach: Compute sum of maxima and sum of minima separately via contribution boundaries, then subtract. Linearity lets every subarray's range decompose this way.
Sum of Subarray Ranges.trace: [1,2] range1, [2,3] range1, [1,2,3] range2; singletons zero; total4.
Sum of Subarray Ranges.pitfalls: Use long before multiplying index spans; extreme unconstrained inputs can still exceed long.

Remove K Digits.problem: Remove exactly k digits preserving order; return the smallest nonnegative decimal number with no leading zeros (zero as "0").
Remove K Digits.approach: A larger preceding digit is worse than the smaller incoming digit at the earliest differing position, so remove it while deletions remain. If digits stay increasing, remaining deletions come from the end.
Remove K Digits.trace: Remove 4 before 3, 3 before 2, and one 2 before 1; resulting 1219.
Remove K Digits.pitfalls: Trim zeros after selecting the sequence, not before counting deletions. All digits removed returns zero.

Next Smaller Element.problem: For each entry return nearest strictly smaller value to its right; absent=-1. Return values, not indices.
Next Smaller Element.approach: Scan backwards; pop candidates that cannot beat the current value. Each popped candidate is also hidden for any future earlier position by the closer current value. A double scan makes one full circular suffix visible.
Next Smaller Element.complexity: O(n) time/space because each pushed entry pops at most once.
Next Smaller Element.trace: For [2,1,3], next greater values are 3,3,none; next smaller are 1,none,none.
Next Smaller Element.pitfalls: Strict comparison requires popping equals. The value -1 is ambiguous for arbitrary signed arrays; indices or OptionalInt can represent absence unambiguously.
Next Smaller Element.alternatives: Scanning each suffix separately takes O(n²) time.

Implement Min Stack.problem: Integer stack with O(1) minimum query; empty removal/minimum throws.
Implement Min Stack.approach: A parallel stack stores the minimum at each depth. Push derives the new prefix minimum; pop removes both depths simultaneously.
Implement Min Stack.trace: Values 3,1,2 store prefix minima 3,1,1; after two pops minimum restores to 3.
Implement Min Stack.pitfalls: Duplicate minima need separate depth entries; this implementation handles them naturally.

Sliding Window Maximum.problem: Return max for each full contiguous window of width k, 1<=k<=n.
Sliding Window Maximum.approach: Deque holds unexpired indices with strictly decreasing values. A newer value at least as large dominates the older one until expiration. Front is always the current maximum.
Sliding Window Maximum.complexity: O(n) time; O(k) deque plus output.
Sliding Window Maximum.trace: Initial window max3; once 5 enters it removes dominated suffix candidates and becomes max.
Sliding Window Maximum.pitfalls: Store indices to test expiration; storing values alone cannot distinguish equal old/new entries.
Sliding Window Maximum.alternatives: Scanning each window costs O(nk); a heap with lazy expiry costs O(n log n) and can grow beyond k.

Trapping Rainwater.problem: Nonnegative bar heights of unit width; compute total trapped water.
Trapping Rainwater.approach: Process the side with the smaller established boundary maximum. Its water level is already limited by that side regardless of unknown interior heights; add max-height and advance.
Trapping Rainwater.trace: Valleys between left/right barriers accumulate six units in the standard example.
Trapping Rainwater.pitfalls: Return long. Empty input holds zero water.
Trapping Rainwater.alternatives: Prefix/suffix maxima use O(n) space; checking boundaries per bar uses O(n²) time.

Largest rectangle in a histogram.problem: Nonnegative unit-width bars; return largest rectangular area fitting below the histogram.
Largest rectangle in a histogram.approach: When a lower/equal bar arrives, pop bars whose right boundary is now known. The new stack top is the nearest smaller left boundary; popped height spans i-left-1 bars.
Largest rectangle in a histogram.pitfalls: Flush at virtual index n without dereferencing a[n]. Area multiplication must be long.

Maximum Rectangles.problem: Largest all-one rectangle area in a rectangular binary matrix.
Maximum Rectangles.approach: Each row is a histogram of consecutive ones ending there. Every all-one rectangle has a bottom row, so maximizing the histogram rectangle at every row considers all candidates.
Maximum Rectangles.trace: At row 2, columns 2..4 each have height at least 2, yielding area 6.
Maximum Rectangles.pitfalls: Reset height to zero on a zero cell; do not sum ones across gaps.

Stock span problem.problem: Online span counts consecutive days ending today whose price<=today, including today.
Stock span problem.approach: Maintain decreasing prices with compressed span counts. Every popped block is entirely dominated by the incoming price, so add its span to the new block.
Stock span problem.complexity: O(1) amortized per next, O(n) worst single call; O(n) storage.
Stock span problem.trace: 75 absorbs 60,70 and their prior covered 60 to get span four.
Stock span problem.pitfalls: Equal prices are included and must pop with <=, not <.

Celebrity Problem.problem: A celebrity knows nobody else and is known by everybody else; return index or -1.
Celebrity Problem.approach: If candidate knows i, candidate cannot be celebrity, so replace with i. Otherwise i cannot be celebrity. One candidate survives; verify both defining conditions.
Celebrity Problem.complexity: O(n) matrix queries and O(1) space excluding input.
Celebrity Problem.trace: Candidate 0 knows 1 -> candidate becomes 1; all others know 1, and 1 knows none.
Celebrity Problem.pitfalls: Elimination alone is insufficient; the verification pass is mandatory. Diagonal values are ignored.

LRU Cache.problem: Least-recently-used eviction; successful get and put refresh recency. OptionalInt means missing.
LRU Cache.approach: Access-order LinkedHashMap maintains oldest at the front and newest at the back; remove its first key when capacity is exceeded.
LRU Cache.trace: After put1,put2,get1 recency is [2,1]; put3 evicts 2.
LRU Cache.pitfalls: Capacity zero stores nothing. This cache is not thread-safe. A handwritten hashmap+doubly-list implementation follows the same recency invariant.

LFU Cache.problem: Least-frequently-used eviction; ties choose least recently used among that frequency. Get and update put increase frequency; new entries start at one.
LFU Cache.approach: Map keys to entries; map each frequency to an insertion-ordered set. Touch moves key to the next frequency group's newest end. minimum tracks the smallest live frequency; evict its oldest key.
LFU Cache.complexity: Expected O(1) get/put, O(capacity) live storage.
LFU Cache.trace: get1 raises its frequency to two; put3 evicts key2 at frequency one.
LFU Cache.pitfalls: Empty groups are removed to bound metadata. Frequency int overflow after billions of accesses is outside this teaching contract; production implementations need an aging/overflow policy.

Number of Greater Elements to the Right.problem: For each index count ALL strictly greater values to its right, not just the next greater.
Number of Greater Elements to the Right.approach: Scan right-to-left, storing seen counts in a Fenwick tree over compressed ranks. Greater count is total seen minus count at ranks<=current.
Number of Greater Elements to the Right.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space, including sorted copy and Fenwick tree.
Number of Greater Elements to the Right.trace: For 3, values 4 and 7 are greater; for 4 only 7; for 2 only 7.
Number of Greater Elements to the Right.pitfalls: Strictly greater excludes equal ranks. Coordinate lookup uses lower bound, so duplicates do not cause a linear rank-search scan.
